items.pronunciationHint: Use the short /ʊ/ sound, not a long “oo.”
items.exampleSentence: This is my book.
items.exampleJapanese: これは私の本です。
items.commonMistake: Do not stretch the vowel as in “moon.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of book.
visual.altJa: 本のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I have a pen.
items.exampleJapanese: 私はペンを持っています。
items.commonMistake: Do not add an extra vowel after the final n.

visual.altEn: An illustration of pen.
visual.altJa: ペンのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Join /s/ and /k/ at the end without a vowel.
items.exampleSentence: This is my desk.
items.exampleJapanese: これは私の机です。
items.commonMistake: Avoid saying “desuku” with extra vowels.

visual.altEn: An illustration of desk.
visual.altJa: 机のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Sit on the chair, please.
items.exampleJapanese: 椅子に座ってください。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the first sound like /ʃ/.

visual.altEn: An illustration of chair.
visual.altJa: 椅子のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: This is my bag.
items.exampleJapanese: これは私のかばんです。
items.commonMistake: Do not make the vowel sound like the one in “bug.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of bag.
visual.altJa: かばんのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Hold the vowel smoothly and finish with a light r in US English.
items.exampleSentence: Please close the door.
items.exampleJapanese: ドアを閉めてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not split it into two strong syllables.

visual.altEn: An illustration of door.
visual.altJa: ドアのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Open the window, please.
items.exampleJapanese: 窓を開けてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not stress the final syllable.

visual.altEn: An illustration of window.
visual.altJa: 窓のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress TEE and use /tʃ/ in the middle.
items.exampleSentence: This is my teacher.
items.exampleJapanese: こちらは私の先生です。
items.commonMistake: Do not use a /ʃ/ sound in the middle.

visual.altEn: An illustration of teacher.
visual.altJa: 先生のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress STU and keep the final t light.
items.exampleSentence: I'm a student.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は生徒です。
items.commonMistake: Do not drop the final t completely.

visual.altEn: A student studying at a desk with a book.
visual.altJa: 机で本を使って勉強している生徒。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress LES; the second vowel is weak.
items.exampleSentence: The lesson starts now.
items.exampleJapanese: 今からレッスンが始まります。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce both syllables with equal stress.

visual.altEn: A teacher and a student learning together in a classroom.
visual.altJa: 教室で先生と生徒が一緒に学んでいます。

items.pronunciationHint: Keep the vowel short and the final d voiced.
items.exampleSentence: I have a red cup.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は赤いカップを持っています。
items.commonMistake: Do not replace the r with an l sound.

visual.altEn: An illustration of red.
visual.altJa: 赤いのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Her shoes are blue.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女の靴は青いです。
items.commonMistake: Do not insert a vowel between b and l.

visual.altEn: An illustration of blue.
visual.altJa: 青いのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The yellow bus is here.
items.exampleJapanese: 黄色いバスが来ました。
items.commonMistake: Do not begin with a Japanese-style strong イ sound.

visual.altEn: An illustration of yellow.
visual.altJa: 黄色いのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The bag is green.
items.exampleJapanese: かばんは緑色です。
items.commonMistake: Do not insert a vowel between g and r.

visual.altEn: An illustration of green.
visual.altJa: 緑ののイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use /æ/ and end with a crisp /k/.
items.exampleSentence: This is a black pen.
items.exampleJapanese: これは黒いペンです。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a vowel after the final k.

visual.altEn: An illustration of black.
visual.altJa: 黒いのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Start with rounded lips for /w/ and finish with t.
items.exampleSentence: The wall is white.
items.exampleJapanese: 壁は白いです。
items.commonMistake: Do not drop the final t.

visual.altEn: An illustration of white.
visual.altJa: 白いのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress CIR; the second syllable is weak.
items.exampleSentence: Draw a circle.
items.exampleJapanese: 丸を描いてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the c as /k/ at the start.

visual.altEn: An illustration of circle.
visual.altJa: 円・丸のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Say the /skw/ cluster as one smooth start.
items.exampleSentence: This shape is a square.
items.exampleJapanese: この形は正方形です。
items.commonMistake: Do not separate s, k, and w with vowels.

visual.altEn: An illustration of square.
visual.altJa: 正方形のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Join /s/ and /t/. US English ends with an r sound; the usual UK model has a long vowel without r.
items.exampleSentence: That star is bright.
items.exampleJapanese: あの星は明るいです。
items.commonMistake: Do not insert a vowel between s and t.

visual.altEn: An illustration of star.
visual.altJa: 星のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Draw a straight line.
items.exampleJapanese: まっすぐな線を描いてください。
items.commonMistake: For the shape, say “draw a line.” “Stand in line” uses the separate meaning of a queue.

visual.altEn: An illustration of line.
visual.altJa: 線のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Voice the middle th /ð/ as in “this.”
items.exampleSentence: My mother likes music.
items.exampleJapanese: 私の母は音楽が好きです。
items.commonMistake: Do not use the unvoiced th from “think.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of mother.
visual.altJa: 母・お母さんのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use a voiced /ð/ in the middle.
items.exampleSentence: My father cooks on Sunday.
items.exampleJapanese: 私の父は日曜日に料理をします。
items.commonMistake: Do not replace th with a z sound.

visual.altEn: An illustration of father.
visual.altJa: 父・お父さんのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress SIS and keep the second vowel weak.
items.exampleSentence: My sister plays tennis.
items.exampleJapanese: 私の姉はテニスをします。
items.commonMistake: Do not strongly pronounce both syllables.

visual.altEn: An illustration of sister.
visual.altJa: 姉・妹のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Blend /b/ and /r/ and voice the th.
items.exampleSentence: Her brother is twelve.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女の弟は12歳です。
items.commonMistake: Do not insert a vowel between b and r.

visual.altEn: An illustration of brother.
visual.altJa: 兄・弟のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress GRAND. In natural speech, the d may be light or absent depending on the speaker.
items.exampleSentence: My grandmother is kind.
items.exampleJapanese: 私の祖母は親切です。
items.commonMistake: Both /ɡrænd-/ and /ɡræn-/ are heard; do not force an extra vowel between the two parts.

visual.altEn: An illustration of grandmother.
visual.altJa: 祖母・おばあさんのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress GRAND. The d is often light or absent before f in natural speech.
items.exampleSentence: My grandfather likes books.
items.exampleJapanese: 私の祖父は本が好きです。
items.commonMistake: Connect “grand” and “father” without a full pause, and use a voiced th in “father.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of grandfather.
visual.altJa: 祖父・おじいさんのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress BAY and use a long /eɪ/.
items.exampleSentence: The baby is sleeping.
items.exampleJapanese: 赤ちゃんは眠っています。
items.commonMistake: Do not make the first vowel short.

visual.altEn: An illustration of baby.
visual.altJa: 赤ちゃんのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Blend /f/ and /r/ and keep the final d.
items.exampleSentence: Mika is my best friend.
items.exampleJapanese: ミカは私の親友です。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a vowel after the final d.

visual.altEn: Two friends holding hands.
visual.altJa: 友達同士が手をつないでいます。

items.exampleSentence: The boy has a blue kite.
items.exampleJapanese: その男の子は青い凧を持っています。
items.commonMistake: Do not split the vowel into two syllables.

visual.altEn: A portrait of a boy.
visual.altJa: 男の子の顔。

items.pronunciationHint: Hold the central vowel and finish with l.
items.exampleSentence: The girl is reading.
items.exampleJapanese: その女の子は本を読んでいます。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a vowel after the final l.

visual.altEn: A portrait of a girl.
visual.altJa: 女の子の顔。

items.exampleSentence: Touch your head.
items.exampleJapanese: 頭を触ってください。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce it like “heed.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of head.
visual.altJa: 頭のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use the long /eɪ/ sound and finish with /s/.
items.exampleSentence: Wash your face.
items.exampleJapanese: 顔を洗ってください。
items.commonMistake: The final sound is /s/, not /z/.

visual.altEn: An illustration of face.
visual.altJa: 顔のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Something is in my eye.
items.exampleJapanese: 目に何か入っています。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a y sound after the word.

visual.altEn: An illustration of eye.
visual.altJa: 目のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Start with a relaxed /ɪ/. US English ends in r; the usual UK model does not pronounce a final r here.
items.exampleSentence: My left ear hurts.
items.exampleJapanese: 左耳が痛いです。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce it the same as “year.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of ear.
visual.altJa: 耳のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The dog has a wet nose.
items.exampleJapanese: その犬は鼻がぬれています。
items.commonMistake: The final sound is /z/, not /s/.

visual.altEn: The nose is highlighted on a face seen from the side.
visual.altJa: 横顔の鼻を丸で示しています。

items.exampleSentence: Open your mouth wide.
items.exampleJapanese: 口を大きく開けてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce it like the computer “mouse.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of mouth.
visual.altJa: 口のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use /æ/ and keep the final d.
items.exampleSentence: Raise your hand.
items.exampleJapanese: 手を挙げてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not drop the final d.

visual.altEn: An illustration of hand.
visual.altJa: 手のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: My right foot is cold.
items.exampleJapanese: 右足が冷たいです。
items.commonMistake: The plural is “feet,” not “foots.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of foot.
visual.altJa: 足・足首から下のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Hold the vowel; pronounce r lightly in US English.
items.exampleSentence: Raise your right arm.
items.exampleJapanese: 右腕を上げてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not confuse “arm” with “hand.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of arm.
visual.altJa: 腕のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use a short /e/ and a firm final g.
items.exampleSentence: My left leg hurts.
items.exampleJapanese: 左脚が痛いです。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a vowel after the final g.

visual.altEn: An illustration of leg.
visual.altJa: 脚のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: We eat rice with dinner.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちは夕食にご飯を食べます。
items.commonMistake: “Rice” is normally uncountable; avoid “a rice.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of rice.
visual.altJa: ご飯・米のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I like bread.
items.exampleJapanese: 私はパンが好きです。
items.commonMistake: “Bread” is uncountable; say “a slice of bread.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of bread.
visual.altJa: パンのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Start with a short /e/ and finish with g.
items.exampleSentence: I have an egg.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は卵を1つ持っています。
items.commonMistake: Use “an,” not “a,” before “egg.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of egg.
visual.altJa: 卵のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Finish with the /lk/ cluster without an extra vowel.
items.exampleSentence: I drink milk.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は牛乳を飲みます。
items.commonMistake: “Milk” is usually uncountable.

visual.altEn: An illustration of milk.
visual.altJa: 牛乳のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: In US speech, the middle t often sounds like a quick d.
items.exampleSentence: Could I have some water?
items.exampleJapanese: お水をいただけますか。
items.commonMistake: Do not say “a water” unless you mean one serving.

visual.altEn: An illustration of water.
visual.altJa: 水のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress AP and use /æ/ at the start.
items.exampleSentence: This apple is green.
items.exampleJapanese: このりんごは緑色です。
items.commonMistake: Use “an apple,” not “a apple.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of apple.
visual.altJa: りんごのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: This banana is very sweet.
items.exampleJapanese: このバナナはとても甘いです。
items.commonMistake: Do not stress the first syllable.

visual.altEn: An illustration of banana.
visual.altJa: バナナのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress CHICK; the second vowel is weak.
items.exampleSentence: I like chicken and rice.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は鶏肉とご飯が好きです。
items.commonMistake: The food is uncountable: “some chicken.” “A chicken” means one bird.

visual.altEn: An illustration of chicken.
visual.altJa: 鶏肉のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The fish is fresh today.
items.exampleJapanese: 今日の魚は新鮮です。
items.commonMistake: The usual plural can be “fish,” not always “fishes.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of fish.
visual.altJa: 魚のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Hold the /uː/ vowel and finish with p.
items.exampleSentence: The soup is hot.
items.exampleJapanese: スープは熱いです。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a vowel after the final p.

visual.altEn: An illustration of soup.
visual.altJa: スープのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Our house is small.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちの家は小さいです。
items.commonMistake: Use “home” for the idea of where you live, not always “house.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of house.
visual.altJa: 家・住宅のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: A long /uː/ is common. Some speakers use a shorter /ʊ/; follow the voice you are practising.
items.exampleSentence: My room is clean.
items.exampleJapanese: 私の部屋はきれいです。
items.commonMistake: Say “in my room,” not “at my room.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of room.
visual.altJa: 部屋のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress KITCH; the final vowel is weak.
items.exampleSentence: Dad is cooking in the kitchen.
items.exampleJapanese: 父は台所で料理をしています。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the t as a separate syllable.

visual.altEn: A room with a cooker, sink, and fridge for preparing food.
visual.altJa: コンロ・流し・冷蔵庫がある台所。

items.exampleSentence: The bathroom is down the hall.
items.exampleJapanese: 浴室は廊下の先です。
items.commonMistake: In US English, “bathroom” may also mean a toilet room.

visual.altEn: A bathroom with a bath, toilet, and washbasin.
visual.altJa: 浴槽・トイレ・洗面台がある浴室。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress BED and connect the two parts.
items.exampleSentence: This is my bedroom.
items.exampleJapanese: ここは私の寝室です。
items.commonMistake: Do not separate “bed” and “room” with a long pause.

visual.altEn: A bed and a bedside lamp in a room with a window.
visual.altJa: 窓のある寝室にベッドとランプがあります。

items.pronunciationHint: Use short /e/ and keep the final d.
items.exampleSentence: My bed is next to the window.
items.exampleJapanese: 私のベッドは窓の隣にあります。
items.commonMistake: Say “go to bed” without “the” for sleeping.

visual.altEn: An illustration of bed.
visual.altJa: ベッドのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress TAY; the second syllable is weak.
items.exampleSentence: Dinner is on the table.
items.exampleJapanese: 夕食はテーブルの上です。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the final e.

visual.altEn: An illustration of table.
visual.altJa: テーブルのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use /æ/ and close both lips for final p.
items.exampleSentence: Turn off the lamp before bed.
items.exampleJapanese: 寝る前にランプを消してください。
items.commonMistake: Do not drop the final p.

visual.altEn: An illustration of lamp.
visual.altJa: ランプのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I cannot find my key.
items.exampleJapanese: 鍵が見つかりません。
items.commonMistake: A key opens a lock. Use “my key” for one, and “my keys” for several.

visual.altEn: An illustration of key.
visual.altJa: 鍵のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Blend /k/ and /l/ and use a short vowel.
items.exampleSentence: The clock is on the wall.
items.exampleJapanese: 時計は壁にあります。
items.commonMistake: Use “watch” for one worn on the wrist.

visual.altEn: An illustration of clock.
visual.altJa: 時計のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use an open vowel and finish with a voiced g.
items.exampleSentence: Our dog loves the park.
items.exampleJapanese: うちの犬は公園が大好きです。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a vowel after the final g.

visual.altEn: An illustration of dog.
visual.altJa: 犬のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use the open /æ/ vowel and a crisp final t.
items.exampleSentence: The cat is under the sofa.
items.exampleJapanese: 猫はソファの下にいます。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce it like “cut.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of cat.
visual.altJa: 猫のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Hold the r-colored vowel in US English.
items.exampleSentence: A bird is singing outside.
items.exampleJapanese: 外で鳥が鳴いています。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a vowel after the final d.

visual.altEn: An illustration of bird.
visual.altJa: 鳥のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress RAB; the second vowel is weak.
items.exampleSentence: The rabbit has long ears.
items.exampleJapanese: そのうさぎは耳が長いです。
items.commonMistake: Do not double the spoken b just because spelling has two.

visual.altEn: An illustration of rabbit.
visual.altJa: うさぎのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Keep the h and finish with /s/.
items.exampleSentence: The horse can run fast.
items.exampleJapanese: 馬は速く走れます。
items.commonMistake: Do not confuse it with “hose”: the vowel and final sound differ, and UK English may not pronounce the r in “horse.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of horse.
visual.altJa: 馬のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The cow is eating grass.
items.exampleJapanese: 牛は草を食べています。
items.commonMistake: Do not stretch it into two syllables.

visual.altEn: An illustration of cow.
visual.altJa: 牛のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Three sheep are near the fence.
items.exampleJapanese: 3匹の羊が柵のそばにいます。
items.commonMistake: The plural is “sheep,” not “sheeps.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of sheep.
visual.altJa: 羊のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use a short /ɪ/ and final voiced g.
items.exampleSentence: The pig is pink.
items.exampleJapanese: 豚はピンク色です。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce it like “peak.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of pig.
visual.altJa: 豚のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress the first syllable: LI-on. Let the second syllable stay light.
items.exampleSentence: The lion is big.
items.exampleJapanese: ライオンは大きいです。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce it as only one syllable.

visual.altEn: An illustration of lion.
visual.altJa: ライオンのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress EL; keep the other syllables lighter.
items.exampleSentence: The elephant has big ears.
items.exampleJapanese: 象は耳が大きいです。
items.commonMistake: Do not stress the final syllable.

visual.altEn: An illustration of elephant.
visual.altJa: 象のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I can run fast.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は速く走れます。
items.commonMistake: The past form is “ran,” not “runned.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of run.
visual.altJa: 走るのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: The l is silent; use a broad vowel.
items.exampleSentence: We walk to school together.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちは一緒に歩いて学校へ行きます。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the written l.

visual.altEn: An illustration of walk.
visual.altJa: 歩くのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Can you jump over this line?
items.exampleJapanese: この線を跳び越えられますか。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a vowel after p.

visual.altEn: An illustration of jump.
visual.altJa: 跳ぶのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use short /ɪ/ and a final t.
items.exampleSentence: Please sit next to me.
items.exampleJapanese: 私の隣に座ってください。
items.commonMistake: Say “sit on a chair” or “sit down.” “Seat” is a different verb: “Please seat the guests.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of sit.
visual.altJa: 座るのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Blend /st/ and keep the final d.
items.exampleSentence: Please stand up.
items.exampleJapanese: 立ってください。
items.commonMistake: “Stand up” is natural when focusing on the movement; “stand” alone can describe the position or give a concise instruction.

visual.altEn: An illustration of stand.
visual.altJa: 立つのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress O; the second vowel is weak.
items.exampleSentence: Open your book, please.
items.exampleJapanese: 本を開いてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not use “open” where “turn on” is needed for a device.

visual.altEn: An illustration of open.
visual.altJa: 開けるのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: As a verb, finish with voiced /z/.
items.exampleSentence: Close the door, please.
items.exampleJapanese: ドアを閉めてください。
items.commonMistake: The adjective “close” meaning near ends with /s/.

visual.altEn: An illustration of close.
visual.altJa: 閉めるのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I read one page every night.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は毎晩1ページ読みます。
items.commonMistake: The past spelling is the same but is pronounced “red.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of read.
visual.altJa: 読むのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Write your name at the top.
items.exampleJapanese: 上に名前を書いてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the initial w.

visual.altEn: An illustration of write.
visual.altJa: 書くのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Listen to the teacher.
items.exampleJapanese: 先生の話を聞いてください。
items.commonMistake: Use “listen to,” not “listen music.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of listen.
visual.altJa: 聞く・耳を傾けるのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I feel happy when we cook together.
items.exampleJapanese: 一緒に料理をすると私はうれしいです。
items.commonMistake: Say “I am happy,” not “I happy.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of happy.
visual.altJa: うれしい・幸せなのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: She felt sad after the movie.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女は映画の後で悲しくなりました。
items.commonMistake: Use “feel sad,” not “feel sadly,” for your condition.

visual.altEn: An illustration of sad.
visual.altJa: 悲しいのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: US English often has one smooth syllable /taɪrd/. UK English may glide through /aɪə/ before d.
items.exampleSentence: We were tired after the long walk.
items.exampleJapanese: 長く歩いた後、私たちは疲れていました。
items.commonMistake: Use “tired” for your feeling and “tiring” for the cause.

visual.altEn: An illustration of tired.
visual.altJa: 疲れたのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress ANG and pronounce the g.
items.exampleSentence: He is angry about the broken toy.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼はおもちゃが壊れたことに怒っています。
items.commonMistake: Use “angry with someone” or “angry about something.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of angry.
visual.altJa: 怒っているのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The child is scared of thunder.
items.exampleJapanese: その子は雷を怖がっています。
items.commonMistake: Say “scared of,” not “scared from.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of scared.
visual.altJa: 怖がっているのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I am excited about the school trip.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は遠足を楽しみにしています。
items.commonMistake: Use “excited” for a person and “exciting” for an event.

visual.altEn: An illustration of excited.
visual.altJa: わくわくしたのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I am hungry after swimming.
items.exampleJapanese: 泳いだ後はお腹が空きます。
items.commonMistake: Say “I am hungry,” not “I have hungry.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of hungry.
visual.altJa: お腹が空いたのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Are you thirsty after practice?
items.exampleJapanese: 練習の後、喉が渇いていますか。
items.commonMistake: Do not replace th with s.

visual.altEn: An illustration of thirsty.
visual.altJa: 喉が渇いたのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use short /ɪ/ and a final k.
items.exampleSentence: I stayed home because I was sick.
items.exampleJapanese: 具合が悪かったので家にいました。
items.commonMistake: In British English, “be sick” can also mean vomit.

visual.altEn: An unwell person with a headache and a thermometer.
visual.altJa: 頭が痛く、体温を測っている具合の悪い人。

items.exampleSentence: I am fine now, thank you.
items.exampleJapanese: 今は大丈夫です、ありがとう。
items.commonMistake: “Fine” can sound merely okay, not always excellent.

visual.altEn: A person feeling well gives a positive sign.
visual.altJa: 元気な人が大丈夫という合図をしています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress SUN; the final y is /i/.
items.exampleSentence: It will be sunny this afternoon.
items.exampleJapanese: 今日の午後は晴れるでしょう。
items.commonMistake: Use “sunny,” not “sun,” after “It is.”

visual.altEn: Sunlight shines on a tree outdoors.
visual.altJa: 屋外の木に太陽の光が当たっています。

items.pronunciationHint: Use the long /eɪ/ in the first syllable.
items.exampleSentence: We need boots on rainy days.
items.exampleJapanese: 雨の日には長靴が必要です。
items.commonMistake: Use “rainy” for weather and “raining” for the action now.

visual.altEn: Rain falls on an open umbrella.
visual.altJa: 開いた傘に雨が降っています。

items.exampleSentence: The sky became cloudy before lunch.
items.exampleJapanese: 昼食前に空が曇りました。
items.commonMistake: Do not use “cloud” directly after “It is.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of cloudy.
visual.altJa: 曇ったのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress WIN; keep the d audible.
items.exampleSentence: It is too windy for a picnic.
items.exampleJapanese: 風が強すぎてピクニックには向きません。
items.commonMistake: Do not confuse “windy” with “winding.”

visual.altEn: Wind bends a tree and blows a scarf sideways.
visual.altJa: 風で木が傾き、マフラーが横になびいています。

items.exampleSentence: The sand is hot in the sun.
items.exampleJapanese: 日なたの砂は熱いです。
items.commonMistake: Use “hot” for temperature, not “high.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of hot.
visual.altJa: 暑い・熱いのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: My hands are cold.
items.exampleJapanese: 手が冷たいです。
items.commonMistake: Say “I am cold” for your feeling, not “I have cold.”

visual.altEn: A person needs a warm coat in falling snow.
visual.altJa: 雪の中で暖かいコートが必要な寒さ。

items.exampleSentence: The evening sky turned pink.
items.exampleJapanese: 夕方の空がピンク色になりました。
items.commonMistake: Use “in the sky,” not usually “on the sky.”

visual.altEn: A bird flies high among clouds, with the open sky highlighted.
visual.altJa: 雲の間を鳥が飛び、広い空が示されています。

items.exampleSentence: The sun rises in the east.
items.exampleJapanese: 太陽は東から昇ります。
items.commonMistake: Use “the sun” with the definite article.

visual.altEn: An illustration of sun.
visual.altJa: 太陽のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The moon looks large tonight.
items.exampleJapanese: 今夜は月が大きく見えます。
items.commonMistake: Use “the moon” when referring to Earth’s moon.

visual.altEn: An illustration of moon.
visual.altJa: 月のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Fresh snow covered the road.
items.exampleJapanese: 新雪が道路を覆いました。
items.commonMistake: “Snow” is usually uncountable; avoid “a snow.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of snow.
visual.altJa: 雪のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress MORN; the ending is weak.
items.exampleSentence: I study English every morning.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は毎朝英語を勉強します。
items.commonMistake: Say “in the morning,” but “this morning” without “in.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of morning.
visual.altJa: 朝のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The meeting is this afternoon.
items.exampleJapanese: 会議は今日の午後です。
items.commonMistake: Do not say “in this afternoon.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of afternoon.
visual.altJa: 午後のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress EVE and keep the middle light.
items.exampleSentence: We take a walk in the evening.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちは夕方に散歩します。
items.commonMistake: Use “in the evening,” but “this evening” without “in.”

visual.altEn: The sun is low behind a house as daylight fades.
visual.altJa: 家の向こうに太陽が沈み、夕方になっています。

items.pronunciationHint: The gh is silent; finish with t.
items.exampleSentence: I read before bed at night.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は夜、寝る前に本を読みます。
items.commonMistake: Say “at night,” not “in night.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of night.
visual.altJa: 夜のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I have plenty of time today.
items.exampleJapanese: 今日は時間がたっぷりあります。
items.commonMistake: Do not add “on” before “today.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of today.
visual.altJa: 今日のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Let us finish this tomorrow.
items.exampleJapanese: これは明日終わらせましょう。
items.commonMistake: Do not add “on” before “tomorrow.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of tomorrow.
visual.altJa: 明日のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress YES and keep the rest lighter.
items.exampleSentence: Yesterday was my day off.
items.exampleJapanese: 昨日は休みでした。
items.commonMistake: Do not use present tense for a finished event yesterday.

visual.altEn: An illustration of yesterday.
visual.altJa: 昨日のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use an r-colored first vowel in US English.
items.exampleSentence: She arrived ten minutes early.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女は10分早く着きました。
items.commonMistake: “Early” is not the same as “fast.”

visual.altEn: A passenger arrives at 8:50 for a bus leaving at 9:00.
visual.altJa: 9時発のバスに8時50分に着く人。

items.exampleSentence: The train is five minutes late.
items.exampleJapanese: 電車は5分遅れています。
items.commonMistake: Use “late for” an event or obligation; “late to class” is also common when focusing on arrival.

visual.altEn: A passenger arrives at 9:10 after the bus left at 9:00.
visual.altJa: 9時発のバスに9時10分に着き、乗り遅れた人。

items.exampleSentence: I am busy until Friday.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は金曜日まで忙しいです。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the s as /s/.

visual.altEn: An illustration of busy.
visual.altJa: 忙しいのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The school is across from the park.
items.exampleJapanese: 学校は公園の向かいです。
items.commonMistake: Say “go to school” without “the” for attending classes.

visual.altEn: An illustration of school.
visual.altJa: 学校のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Keep the p unvoiced and use the r in US English.
items.exampleSentence: We met near the park gate.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちは公園の門の近くで会いました。
items.commonMistake: Do not confuse “park” the place with “park” a vehicle.

visual.altEn: A green public park with a tree, grass, and a bench.
visual.altJa: 木と芝生、ベンチがある公園。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress STAY and use /ʃ/ before the ending.
items.exampleSentence: Which station is next?
items.exampleJapanese: 次はどの駅ですか。
items.commonMistake: Use “at the station,” not “in station.”

visual.altEn: A train beside a station sign and departure clock.
visual.altJa: 駅の看板と時計のそばに電車が停まっています。

items.exampleSentence: That store closes at eight.
items.exampleJapanese: あの店は8時に閉まります。
items.commonMistake: British English often uses “shop” where US English uses “store.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of store.
visual.altJa: 店のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress HOS; later syllables are lighter.
items.exampleSentence: The hospital is beside the bank.
items.exampleJapanese: 病院は銀行の隣です。
items.commonMistake: Use “go to the hospital” in US English for a visit.

visual.altEn: A medical building with a doctor welcoming patients.
visual.altJa: 医療の建物で医師が患者を迎えています。

items.pronunciationHint: Usually three syllables: LI-brar-y, with the stress on LI.
items.exampleSentence: You can borrow this at the library.
items.exampleJapanese: これは図書館で借りられます。
items.commonMistake: Keep the r after b clear; some speakers reduce the middle syllable in fast speech.

visual.altEn: A reader sits beside shelves of books in a quiet library.
visual.altJa: 本棚のそばで読書をしている図書館の場面。

items.exampleSentence: This restaurant serves vegetable curry.
items.exampleJapanese: このレストランでは野菜カレーを出します。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce every written vowel equally.

visual.altEn: A waiter serves a meal at a dining table.
visual.altJa: 食卓で店員が料理を出しているレストランの場面。

items.exampleSentence: The bank is closed today.
items.exampleJapanese: 銀行は今日休みです。
items.commonMistake: Do not add a vowel after k.

visual.altEn: An illustration of bank.
visual.altJa: 銀行のイラスト。

items.kanaReading: ポウスト オフィス
items.pronunciationHint: Keep the final t in “post” before “office.”
items.exampleSentence: I mailed the parcel at the post office.
items.exampleJapanese: 郵便局で小包を送りました。
items.commonMistake: Write it as two words, not one.

visual.altEn: A postal worker helps a customer send a letter.
visual.altJa: 郵便局の職員が手紙を送る人を手伝っています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress PLAY and connect both parts smoothly.
items.exampleSentence: The children are on the playground.
items.exampleJapanese: 子どもたちは遊び場にいます。
items.commonMistake: US English often uses “on the playground”; UK English commonly uses “in the playground.”

visual.altEn: A playground with a slide and someone on a swing.
visual.altJa: すべり台とブランコのある遊び場。

items.pronunciationHint: Use the r-colored vowel /ɝː/ in US English.
items.exampleSentence: This shirt fits me well.
items.exampleJapanese: このシャツは私によく合います。
items.commonMistake: A shirt normally has a collar or buttons; a T-shirt is different.

visual.altEn: An illustration of shirt.
visual.altJa: シャツのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: These pants are too long.
items.exampleJapanese: このズボンは長すぎます。
items.commonMistake: US “pants” means trousers; UK “pants” usually means underwear. For this item, practise the US clothing meaning: “these pants.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of pants.
visual.altJa: ズボンのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: She wore a blue dress.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女は青いワンピースを着ていました。
items.commonMistake: English “dress” is not every type of clothing.

visual.altEn: An illustration of dress.
visual.altJa: ワンピース・ドレスのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Blend /sk/ and keep the final t.
items.exampleSentence: This skirt has two pockets.
items.exampleJapanese: このスカートにはポケットが2つあります。
items.commonMistake: Do not drop the final t.

visual.altEn: An illustration of skirt.
visual.altJa: スカートのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Please leave your shoes by the door.
items.exampleJapanese: 靴をドアのそばに置いてください。
items.commonMistake: Use the plural “shoes” for a pair.

visual.altEn: An illustration of shoes.
visual.altJa: 靴のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: My socks are still wet.
items.exampleJapanese: 靴下はまだぬれています。
items.commonMistake: Use “a pair of socks,” not “a socks.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of socks.
visual.altJa: 靴下のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Take your hat off indoors.
items.exampleJapanese: 室内では帽子を取ってください。
items.commonMistake: “Hat” usually has a brim or shaped crown; “cap” is more specific.

visual.altEn: An illustration of hat.
visual.altJa: 帽子のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use /oʊ/ and keep the final t.
items.exampleSentence: Bring a warm coat tonight.
items.exampleJapanese: 今夜は暖かいコートを持ってきてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not drop the final t.

visual.altEn: An illustration of coat.
visual.altJa: コート・上着のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I need gloves for the snow.
items.exampleJapanese: 雪の日には手袋が必要です。
items.commonMistake: Use the plural for the usual pair.

visual.altEn: An illustration of gloves.
visual.altJa: 手袋のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I left my umbrella on the train.
items.exampleJapanese: 電車に傘を忘れました。
items.commonMistake: Use “an umbrella,” not “a umbrella.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of umbrella.
visual.altJa: 傘のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use a strong r in US English and a long vowel in UK English.
items.exampleSentence: We rented a small car.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちは小型車を借りました。
items.commonMistake: Say “by car,” but “in the car.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of car.
visual.altJa: 車のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Use the short /ʌ/ vowel and final /s/.
items.exampleSentence: The bus comes every twenty minutes.
items.exampleJapanese: そのバスは20分ごとに来ます。
items.commonMistake: The plural is “buses,” not “bus.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of bus.
visual.altJa: バスのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I caught the last train home.
items.exampleJapanese: 最終電車で帰りました。
items.commonMistake: Say “by train,” but “on the train.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of train.
visual.altJa: 電車のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress BI and make the middle c sound /s/.
items.exampleSentence: He rides his bicycle to work.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼は自転車で通勤します。
items.commonMistake: “Ride a bicycle,” not “drive a bicycle.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of bicycle.
visual.altJa: 自転車のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress AIR and connect both parts.
items.exampleSentence: The airplane landed safely.
items.exampleJapanese: 飛行機は無事に着陸しました。
items.commonMistake: Use “on the airplane,” not “in airplane.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of airplane.
visual.altJa: 飛行機のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Let us take a taxi to the hotel.
items.exampleJapanese: ホテルまでタクシーで行きましょう。
items.commonMistake: Say “take a taxi,” not “ride taxi.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of taxi.
visual.altJa: タクシーのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: We crossed the lake by boat.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちはボートで湖を渡りました。
items.commonMistake: Do not drop the final t.

visual.altEn: An illustration of boat.
visual.altJa: ボートのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress TICK; the second vowel is weak.
items.exampleSentence: Keep your ticket until you leave.
items.exampleJapanese: 出るまで切符を持っていてください。
items.commonMistake: Use “a ticket to Tokyo” for the destination, and “a ticket for the ten o’clock train” for a particular service.

visual.altEn: A train ticket with an origin, destination, and departure time.
visual.altJa: 出発地・目的地・時刻が書かれた電車の切符。

items.exampleSentence: The map shows a shorter route.
items.exampleJapanese: その地図にはもっと短い道が載っています。
items.commonMistake: Say “on the map,” not “in the map.”

visual.altEn: A map shows roads linking a house, school, and park.
visual.altJa: 家・学校・公園を道路で結ぶ地図。

items.exampleSentence: Our class trip was fun.
items.exampleJapanese: 修学旅行は楽しかったです。
items.commonMistake: Use “trip” for the whole journey; “travel” is usually uncountable.

visual.altEn: Someone packs a suitcase, travels by train, and arrives at a new place.
visual.altJa: 荷造りをして電車に乗り、旅行先に着く流れ。

items.exampleSentence: I clean the kitchen after dinner.
items.exampleJapanese: 夕食後に台所を掃除します。
items.commonMistake: “Clean the kitchen” focuses on making it clean. “Clean up the kitchen” can also include tidying it.

visual.altEn: An illustration of clean.
visual.altJa: 掃除する・清潔なのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Wash your hands before eating.
items.exampleJapanese: 食べる前に手を洗ってください。
items.commonMistake: Use “wash” with water; “clean” is broader.

visual.altEn: An illustration of wash.
visual.altJa: 洗うのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Can you cook rice for four people?
items.exampleJapanese: 4人分のご飯を炊けますか。
items.commonMistake: “Cook” is the action; “a cook” is a person.

visual.altEn: An illustration of cook.
visual.altJa: 料理するのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Please sweep the floor before guests arrive.
items.exampleJapanese: お客さんが来る前に床を掃いてください。
items.commonMistake: The past form is “swept,” not “sweeped.”

visual.altEn: A broom sweeps loose dirt into a small pile.
visual.altJa: ほうきで床のごみを一か所に掃き集めています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress CAR; the final y is /i/.
items.exampleSentence: Could you carry this box upstairs?
items.exampleJapanese: この箱を2階まで運んでもらえますか。
items.commonMistake: “Carry” describes holding and moving something. “Bring” and “take” also tell us about the direction of movement.

visual.altEn: An illustration of carry.
visual.altJa: 運ぶ・持ち歩くのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I need to fix the loose handle.
items.exampleJapanese: 緩んだ取っ手を直す必要があります。
items.commonMistake: Use “fix” directly with the problem or broken object: “fix the handle,” not “fix to the handle.”

visual.altEn: Tools repair a loose part of a car.
visual.altJa: 工具を使って車の緩んだ部分を直しています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress BOR; the ending is weak.
items.exampleSentence: May I borrow your charger?
items.exampleJapanese: 充電器を借りてもいいですか。
items.commonMistake: “Borrow” means receive temporarily; “lend” means give temporarily.

visual.altEn: A book is lent for a short time and then returned.
visual.altJa: 本をしばらく借りてから返す流れ。

items.exampleSentence: Please return the key by Friday.
items.exampleJapanese: 金曜日までに鍵を返してください。
items.commonMistake: Use “return the key,” not “return back the key.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of return.
visual.altJa: 返す・戻るのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Choose the answer that sounds natural.
items.exampleJapanese: 自然に聞こえる答えを選んでください。
items.commonMistake: The past form is “chose”; “chosen” needs an auxiliary.

visual.altEn: A person points to one fruit from two available choices.
visual.altJa: りんごとバナナの中から一つを指して選ぶ人。

items.exampleSentence: I packed a light jacket for the trip.
items.exampleJapanese: 旅行用に薄い上着を詰めました。
items.commonMistake: “Pack a bag” means put things in it. “Pack up” can mean collect your things before leaving.

visual.altEn: An illustration of pack.
visual.altJa: 荷造りするのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Please ask if anything is unclear.
items.exampleJapanese: 分からないことがあれば尋ねてください。
items.commonMistake: The useful everyday pattern is “ask someone a question.” Use “ask for help” when you want assistance.

visual.altEn: An illustration of ask.
visual.altJa: 尋ねる・頼むのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Could you answer the final question?
items.exampleJapanese: 最後の質問に答えてもらえますか。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the written w.

visual.altEn: An illustration of answer.
visual.altJa: 答える・答えのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Can you explain that rule again?
items.exampleJapanese: そのルールをもう一度説明してもらえますか。
items.commonMistake: Say “explain it to me,” not “explain me it.”

visual.altEn: A teacher shows how puzzle pieces fit while a learner follows.
visual.altJa: 先生がパズルの仕組みを説明し、生徒が聞いています。

items.exampleSentence: Please repeat the address slowly.
items.exampleJapanese: 住所をもう一度ゆっくり言ってください。
items.commonMistake: Say “repeat the word,” not “repeat to the word.” “Repeat it again” is possible when another repetition is needed.

visual.altEn: A speaker says the same short message twice to a listener.
visual.altJa: 話し手が聞き手に同じ短い言葉を二度伝えます。

items.exampleSentence: Could you speak a little more slowly?
items.exampleJapanese: もう少しゆっくり話してもらえますか。
items.commonMistake: Use “speak to someone,” not normally “speak someone.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of speak.
visual.altJa: 話すのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: The wh begins like /w/; stress WHIS.
items.exampleSentence: She whispered the answer to me.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女は私に答えをささやきました。
items.commonMistake: Say “whisper to someone,” not “whisper someone.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of whisper.
visual.altJa: ささやくのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Do not shout across the room.
items.exampleJapanese: 部屋の向こうに向かって叫ばないでください。
items.commonMistake: Use “shout at” for anger and “shout to” for distance.

visual.altEn: An illustration of shout.
visual.altJa: 叫ぶのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Hold the vowel and finish with l.
items.exampleSentence: I will call you after work.
items.exampleJapanese: 仕事の後で電話します。
items.commonMistake: Do not add “to” before the person: say “call me.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of call.
visual.altJa: 電話する・呼ぶのイラスト。

items.japanese: メッセージを送る・伝言
items.pronunciationHint: Stress MES; the final age sounds /ɪdʒ/.
items.exampleSentence: Message me when you arrive.
items.exampleJapanese: 着いたらメッセージを送ってください。
items.commonMistake: As a verb, say “message me,” not “message to me.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of message.
visual.altJa: メッセージを送る・伝言のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: We invited our neighbors to dinner.
items.exampleJapanese: 近所の人たちを夕食に招きました。
items.commonMistake: Use “invite someone to a party.” With a meal, both “invite someone to dinner” and “invite someone for dinner” occur.

visual.altEn: A party invitation is sent to a friend, inviting them to join.
visual.altJa: パーティーに来てほしい友達へ招待状を送っています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress HOME and connect both parts.
items.exampleSentence: I put off my homework until the last minute.
items.exampleJapanese: 私はぎりぎりまで宿題を後回しにしました。
items.commonMistake: “Homework” is uncountable; avoid “homeworks.”

visual.altEn: A learner works on a worksheet at home after class.
visual.altJa: 授業後に家でプリントの課題をしている生徒。

items.exampleSentence: Ask a follow-up question if the answer is unclear.
items.exampleJapanese: 答えがはっきりしなければ、追加で質問してください。
items.commonMistake: Use “ask a question,” not “say a question.”

visual.altEn: A learner points to a question mark on a worksheet.
visual.altJa: 生徒がプリントの疑問点を尋ねています。

items.exampleSentence: I keep track of new words in a notebook.
items.exampleJapanese: 私は新しい単語をノートに記録しています。
items.commonMistake: English “notebook” is a bound writing book, not any memo.

visual.altEn: An illustration of notebook.
visual.altJa: ノートのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress DIC; keep later vowels light.
items.exampleSentence: Look the word up in a dictionary, then make your own sentence.
items.exampleJapanese: 辞書でその単語を調べてから、自分で文を作ってください。
items.commonMistake: Say “look up a word in a dictionary,” not “search a word.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of dictionary.
visual.altJa: 辞書のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Which subject would you like to get better at?
items.exampleJapanese: どの科目がもっと得意になりたいですか。
items.commonMistake: Do not confuse a school subject with a lesson period.

visual.altEn: Mathematics, science, and English are different school subjects.
visual.altJa: 算数・理科・英語という異なる科目。

items.exampleSentence: Her writing grade improved this term.
items.exampleJapanese: 今学期、彼女の作文の成績が上がりました。
items.commonMistake: “Grade” can mean a score or school year depending on context.

visual.altEn: A marked worksheet shows a score of eight out of ten.
visual.altJa: 採点済みのプリントに10点中8点の成績が示されています。

items.exampleSentence: We have a listening test tomorrow.
items.exampleJapanese: 明日はリスニングテストがあります。
items.commonMistake: Use “take a test,” not “receive a test,” for sitting an exam.

visual.altEn: An illustration of test.
visual.altJa: テスト・試験のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Daily practice makes speaking easier.
items.exampleJapanese: 毎日の練習で話すことが楽になります。
items.commonMistake: In UK spelling, the verb is often “practise,” while the noun is “practice.”

visual.altEn: A learner tries writing more than once and gets better.
visual.altJa: 繰り返し書く練習をして、できるようになっていく生徒。

items.japanese: 覚えている・思い出す
items.exampleSentence: Remember to bring your workbook.
items.exampleJapanese: ワークブックを持ってくるのを忘れないでください。
items.commonMistake: “Remember to do” is future duty; “remember doing” recalls the past.

visual.altEn: A person recalls their key in a thought bubble.
visual.altJa: 人が頭の中で鍵を思い出しています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress PROVE and finish with voiced v.
items.exampleSentence: Reading aloud can improve your rhythm.
items.exampleJapanese: 音読すると話すリズムがよくなります。
items.commonMistake: Use “improve something” without “to.”

visual.altEn: Regular reading accompanies a steadily rising progress chart.
visual.altJa: 読書を続け、上達のグラフが少しずつ上がっています。

items.exampleSentence: I work from home twice a week and spend the other days at the office.
items.exampleJapanese: 週に2日は在宅で働き、ほかの日はオフィスで働きます。
items.commonMistake: Say “at the office” for your workplace location.

visual.altEn: An illustration of office.
visual.altJa: オフィス・事務所のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: The meeting starts in five minutes.
items.exampleJapanese: 会議は5分後に始まります。
items.commonMistake: Use “have a meeting,” not “do a meeting.”

visual.altEn: People gather around shared work at an agreed time.
visual.altJa: 予定した時刻に集まり、相談している人たち。

items.pronunciationHint: US often begins /sk/; UK often begins /ʃ/.
items.exampleSentence: My schedule is full on Thursday.
items.exampleJapanese: 木曜日は予定がいっぱいです。
items.commonMistake: Both common pronunciations are acceptable; stay consistent.

visual.altEn: A weekly calendar contains several appointments with times.
visual.altJa: 週間カレンダーに時刻付きの予定が並んでいます。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress CUS; later vowels are weak.
items.exampleSentence: The customer asked for a receipt.
items.exampleJapanese: お客さまは領収書を求めました。
items.commonMistake: A “customer” buys; a “client” often receives professional services.

visual.altEn: A person pays for something in a shop.
visual.altJa: 店で商品にお金を払っているお客さん。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress MAN and make g sound /dʒ/.
items.exampleSentence: The manager approved my day off.
items.exampleJapanese: 上司は私の休暇を承認しました。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the g as in “go.”

visual.altEn: One person coordinates the work of a small team.
visual.altJa: 一人がチームの仕事をまとめ、担当を伝えています。

items.exampleSentence: Our project needs a clearer goal.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちのプロジェクトにはもっと明確な目標が必要です。
items.commonMistake: The verb “project” has stress on the second syllable.

visual.altEn: A team turns separate tasks into a finished result over several days.
visual.altJa: 何日かかけて作業を組み合わせ、一つの成果を完成させます。

items.exampleSentence: Please send the report by noon.
items.exampleJapanese: 正午までに報告書を送ってください。
items.commonMistake: Use “write a report on the results.” As a verb, “report to the manager” identifies the person you report to.

visual.altEn: A document combines written findings with a chart.
visual.altJa: 文章とグラフで調べた結果をまとめた報告書。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress DEAD and connect both parts.
items.exampleSentence: The deadline is next Wednesday.
items.exampleJapanese: 締め切りは次の水曜日です。
items.commonMistake: Say “meet a deadline,” not “keep a deadline.”

visual.altEn: A task must be handed in by Friday at three.
visual.altJa: 金曜日の3時までに提出する必要がある課題。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress COL, then use /iː/ and finish with /ɡ/.
items.exampleSentence: A colleague helped me check the figures.
items.exampleJapanese: 同僚が数字の確認を手伝ってくれました。
items.commonMistake: A colleague is someone you work with; “classmate” is someone in your class.

visual.altEn: Two people doing work alongside each other.
visual.altJa: 一緒の職場で働く二人。

items.exampleSentence: Let us take a short break.
items.exampleJapanese: 短い休憩を取りましょう。
items.commonMistake: Use “take a break,” not “do a break.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of break.
visual.altJa: 休憩・壊すのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress DOC; the ending is weak.
items.exampleSentence: The doctor asked about my symptoms.
items.exampleJapanese: 医師は私の症状について尋ねました。
items.commonMistake: Use “see a doctor,” not “meet a doctor,” for medical care.

visual.altEn: An illustration of doctor.
visual.altJa: 医師のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress MED. Speakers may use two syllables or a light middle syllable; do not stress the ending.
items.exampleSentence: Take this medicine after breakfast.
items.exampleJapanese: この薬を朝食後に飲んでください。
items.commonMistake: Say “take medicine,” not “drink medicine” generally.

visual.altEn: An illustration of medicine.
visual.altJa: 薬のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: He has a slight fever.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼には微熱があります。
items.commonMistake: Say “have a fever,” not “be fever.”

visual.altEn: A person feels hot and a thermometer shows a raised temperature.
visual.altJa: 体が熱く、体温計に高い体温が表示されています。

items.exampleSentence: Her cough is getting better.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女のせきはよくなっています。
items.commonMistake: As a verb, say “cough,” not “do a cough.”

visual.altEn: A person covers their mouth while coughing.
visual.altJa: 口を覆いながらせきをしている人。

items.exampleSentence: I have a headache from the bright screen.
items.exampleJapanese: 明るい画面のせいで頭が痛いです。
items.commonMistake: Say “have a headache,” not “my head is headache.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of headache.
visual.altJa: 頭痛のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: You should rest this afternoon.
items.exampleJapanese: 今日の午後は休んだほうがいいです。
items.commonMistake: “Get some rest” is very common; “take a rest” is also natural in some varieties and contexts.

visual.altEn: An illustration of rest.
visual.altJa: 休む・休息のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: A healthy breakfast gives me energy.
items.exampleJapanese: 健康的な朝食で元気が出ます。
items.commonMistake: Use “healthy” for a person or habit; “healthful” is less common.

visual.altEn: An illustration of healthy.
visual.altJa: 健康なのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress EX; the final s sounds /z/.
items.exampleSentence: Gentle exercise helps my back.
items.exampleJapanese: 軽い運動は腰に良いです。
items.commonMistake: “Exercise” can be countable for a task, uncountable for activity.

visual.altEn: An illustration of exercise.
visual.altJa: 運動・練習するのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I felt a sharp pain in my shoulder.
items.exampleJapanese: 肩に鋭い痛みを感じました。
items.commonMistake: Use “pain in my shoulder,” not “pain of my shoulder.”

visual.altEn: A red pulse highlights a sore part of an arm.
visual.altJa: 腕の痛い部分が赤いしるしで示されています。

items.exampleSentence: I made a dentist appointment for Monday.
items.exampleJapanese: 月曜日に歯医者の予約を取りました。
items.commonMistake: Say “make an appointment,” not “reserve a doctor.”

visual.altEn: A calendar marks an agreed time to see a doctor.
visual.altJa: カレンダーに医師と会う予約時刻が入っています。

items.exampleSentence: The price includes tax.
items.exampleJapanese: 価格には税金が含まれています。
items.commonMistake: “Price” is the amount asked; “cost” can be the amount paid.

visual.altEn: A price tag on a coat shows the amount the shop asks for.
visual.altJa: コートの値札に店が提示した値段が書かれています。

items.pronunciationHint: Use a short vowel and final /st/.
items.exampleSentence: How much does delivery cost?
items.exampleJapanese: 配送料はいくらかかりますか。
items.commonMistake: Ask “How much does it cost?” not “How much is the cost?” in casual speech.

visual.altEn: The cost combines the item price and a delivery charge.
visual.altJa: 商品の代金と配送料を合わせた費用。

items.exampleSentence: Can I pay in cash?
items.exampleJapanese: 現金で払えますか。
items.commonMistake: Say “pay in cash” or “pay cash,” not “pay by cash.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of cash.
visual.altJa: 現金のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Here is your change.
items.exampleJapanese: こちらがおつりです。
items.commonMistake: “Change” is uncountable when it means coins or money returned.

visual.altEn: A buyer pays ¥1,000 for a ¥700 item and receives ¥300 back.
visual.altJa: 700円の商品に1,000円を払い、300円のおつりを受け取ります。

items.pronunciationHint: The p is silent; stress CEIPT.
items.exampleSentence: Would you like a receipt?
items.exampleJapanese: レシートは必要ですか。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the written p.

visual.altEn: A receipt lists a purchased item, its price, and the total paid.
visual.altJa: 購入品と値段、支払合計が書かれたレシート。

items.exampleSentence: This coupon gives a ten-percent discount.
items.exampleJapanese: このクーポンで10パーセント割引になります。
items.commonMistake: Say “a discount on an item,” not “discount of an item.”

visual.altEn: The price of the same shirt falls from ¥2,000 to ¥1,500.
visual.altJa: 同じシャツの値段が2,000円から1,500円に下がります。

items.exampleSentence: Do you have this in a larger size?
items.exampleJapanese: これのもっと大きいサイズはありますか。
items.commonMistake: Use “What size?” rather than “Which size are you?”

visual.altEn: Small and large versions of the same clothing item.
visual.altJa: 同じ服の小さいサイズと大きいサイズ。

items.exampleSentence: The bag was cheap but sturdy.
items.exampleJapanese: そのかばんは安いけれど丈夫でした。
items.commonMistake: “Cheap” can imply low quality; use “inexpensive” for a neutral tone.

visual.altEn: A bag has a low price tag.
visual.altJa: かばんに安い値札がついています。

items.exampleSentence: That jacket is too expensive for me.
items.exampleJapanese: その上着は私には高すぎます。
items.commonMistake: Say “expensive,” not “high price” as an adjective.

visual.altEn: A coat has a high price that requires much more money.
visual.altJa: コートに高い値札がつき、たくさんのお金が必要です。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress OR; pronounce r in US English.
items.exampleSentence: I ordered the soup without onions.
items.exampleJapanese: スープを玉ねぎ抜きで注文しました。
items.commonMistake: Use “order something,” not “order for something.”

visual.altEn: A customer asks a waiter for a bowl of soup.
visual.altJa: お客さんが店員にスープを注文しています。

items.exampleSentence: Our neighbor watered the plants for us.
items.exampleJapanese: 近所の人が代わりに植物へ水をやってくれました。
items.commonMistake: US spelling is “neighbor”; UK spelling is “neighbour.”

visual.altEn: People greet each other from two neighbouring houses.
visual.altJa: 隣り合う家の住人があいさつしています。

items.pronunciationHint: The u is silent; start with hard g.
items.exampleSentence: We introduced each guest by name so nobody felt left out.
items.exampleJapanese: 誰も取り残されたと感じないように、一人ずつ名前でお客さんを紹介しました。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the written u.

visual.altEn: A visitor waits at someone else’s front door.
visual.altJa: 招かれた人が訪問先の玄関に立っています。

items.exampleSentence: The host introduced everyone.
items.exampleJapanese: 主催者が全員を紹介しました。
items.commonMistake: A host welcomes guests; it does not mean every event worker.

visual.altEn: A host welcomes a visitor and offers food.
visual.altJa: 迎える側の人が訪問客に食事を出しています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress PART; the second vowel is weak.
items.exampleSentence: Check with your partner before making the final decision.
items.exampleJapanese: 最終的な決定をする前に、一緒に取り組む相手に確認してください。
items.commonMistake: “Partner” does not always mean a romantic partner.

visual.altEn: Two learning partners work on a page together.
visual.altJa: 二人の学習相手が一緒に課題に取り組んでいます。

items.exampleSentence: Our team solved the problem together.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちのチームは一緒に問題を解決しました。
items.commonMistake: Say “on a team” in US English, often “in a team” in UK English.

visual.altEn: Several people combine their work to complete one shared puzzle.
visual.altJa: 何人かが協力して一つのパズルを完成させます。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress PROM; the final s is /s/.
items.exampleSentence: I promise to return it tomorrow.
items.exampleJapanese: 明日返すと約束します。
items.commonMistake: Use “promise to do,” not “promise doing.”

visual.altEn: A handshake and a marked date show a commitment to a future action.
visual.altJa: 握手と予定の日付で、これからすることを約束しています。

items.exampleSentence: It takes time to build trust.
items.exampleJapanese: 信頼を築くには時間がかかります。
items.commonMistake: “Trust someone” is the direct everyday pattern. “Trust in someone” can express strong faith and is also correct.

visual.altEn: A person lets a helper guide them while their eyes are closed.
visual.altJa: 目を閉じた人が、信頼する相手の案内に身を任せています。

items.exampleSentence: Thank you for your support this week.
items.exampleJapanese: 今週支えてくれてありがとう。
items.commonMistake: “Support” is usually uncountable as help.

visual.altEn: An illustration of support.
visual.altJa: 支援・支えるのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress SPECT in both the noun and the verb.
items.exampleSentence: We respect each other’s opinions.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちは互いの意見を尊重します。
items.commonMistake: Use “respect someone,” without “to.”

visual.altEn: One person listens attentively while another gives an opinion.
visual.altJa: 相手の意見を大切にして、注意深く聞いている人。

items.exampleSentence: Her advice helped me decide.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女の助言が決断の助けになりました。
items.commonMistake: “Advice” is uncountable; say “a piece of advice.”

visual.altEn: Someone points out a helpful route to a person deciding where to go.
visual.altJa: 行き方に迷う人へ、役立つ道を示して助言しています。

items.japanese: 利用できる・都合がつく
items.pronunciationHint: Stress VAIL; later syllables are light.
items.exampleSentence: Is this room available after three?
items.exampleJapanese: この部屋は3時以降空いていますか。
items.commonMistake: For people, “available” means free to meet, not always single.

visual.altEn: One chair is occupied while the other is free to use.
visual.altJa: 一方の椅子は使用中、もう一方は空いています。

items.exampleSentence: The later train is more convenient for me.
items.exampleJapanese: 後の電車のほうが私には便利です。
items.commonMistake: Say “The time is convenient for me.” To describe your own availability, say “I’m free,” not “I’m convenient.”

visual.altEn: A station is a short easy walk from home.
visual.altJa: 家から駅まで歩いてすぐで便利な場面。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress POS; the ending is weak.
items.exampleSentence: Is it possible to change the date?
items.exampleJapanese: 日付を変更することは可能ですか。
items.commonMistake: Use “It is possible to change it.” For personal ability, use “I can change it,” not “I am possible to change it.”

visual.altEn: The last puzzle piece fits the gap, showing that the task can be done.
visual.altJa: 最後のピースが空所に合い、完成できることを示しています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress NES; keep later syllables light.
items.exampleSentence: A reservation is not necessary today.
items.exampleJapanese: 今日は予約は必要ありません。
items.commonMistake: Spell it with one c and two s letters.

visual.altEn: A locked door cannot be opened until the matching key is used.
visual.altJa: 閉じたドアを開けるために鍵が必要です。

items.japanese: 確信している・確かな
items.pronunciationHint: The t is often softened; stress CER.
items.exampleSentence: I am certain that I locked the door.
items.exampleJapanese: ドアに鍵をかけたことは確かです。
items.commonMistake: “Certain” is stronger than “probably.”

visual.altEn: A person clearly remembers locking the door and is sure about it.
visual.altJa: ドアに鍵をかけたことをはっきり覚え、確信しています。

items.japanese: よく知っている・見覚えのある
items.exampleSentence: This song sounds familiar.
items.exampleJapanese: この曲は聞き覚えがあります。
items.commonMistake: Say “familiar with something,” not “familiar to something” for your knowledge.

visual.altEn: Hearing a tune brings back a clear memory of the same tune.
visual.altJa: 聞いた曲が記憶とつながり、聞き覚えがあると感じています。

items.exampleSentence: It is polite to wait your turn.
items.exampleJapanese: 順番を待つのは礼儀正しいことです。
items.commonMistake: “Polite” describes behavior; “kind” describes caring.

visual.altEn: Someone opens the door for a visitor and lets them go first.
visual.altJa: 訪問客のためにドアを開け、先にどうぞと案内します。

items.pronunciationHint: The h is silent; stress HON.
items.exampleSentence: Please give me an honest answer.
items.exampleJapanese: 正直な答えをください。
items.commonMistake: Use “honest with someone” and “honest about something.”

visual.altEn: A person admits that they broke the object rather than hiding it.
visual.altJa: 物を壊したことを隠さず、自分だと伝える人。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress PA and pronounce ti as /ʃ/.
items.exampleSentence: Our instructor was patient with beginners.
items.exampleJapanese: 先生は初心者に辛抱強く接しました。
items.commonMistake: As an adjective, say “be patient with someone.” “A patient” is a different meaning: a person receiving medical care.

visual.altEn: A person waits calmly without rushing anyone.
visual.altJa: 相手を急がせず、落ち着いて待っている人。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress CARE; the ending is weak.
items.exampleSentence: Be careful not to share the wrong file.
items.exampleJapanese: 間違ったファイルを共有しないように気をつけてください。
items.commonMistake: Say “careful with” an object and “careful about” a decision.

visual.altEn: A person slowly carries a hot drink, watching not to spill it.
visual.altJa: こぼさないように熱い飲み物を慎重に運んでいます。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress RIVE and finish with voiced v.
items.exampleSentence: We arrived at the venue before noon.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちは正午前に会場へ着きました。
items.commonMistake: Use “arrive at” a place and “arrive in” a city or country.

visual.altEn: An illustration of arrive.
visual.altJa: 到着するのイラスト。

items.japanese: 出発する・置いていく
items.pronunciationHint: Hold /iː/ and finish with voiced v.
items.exampleSentence: The first bus leaves at six.
items.exampleJapanese: 始発バスは6時に出ます。
items.commonMistake: “Leave” can mean depart or intentionally/accidentally keep something behind.

visual.altEn: An illustration of leave.
visual.altJa: 出発する・置いていくのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I missed the train by one minute.
items.exampleJapanese: 1分差で電車に乗り遅れました。
items.commonMistake: Say “miss the bus,” not “miss to the bus.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of miss.
visual.altJa: 逃す・恋しく思うのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: We can catch the express train.
items.exampleJapanese: 急行電車に間に合います。
items.commonMistake: The past form is “caught,” not “catched.”

visual.altEn: A person runs to a bus and gets on before it leaves.
visual.altJa: バスへ走り、出発前に乗れた人。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress CAN; the second vowel is weak.
items.exampleSentence: They canceled the outdoor event.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼らは屋外イベントを中止しました。
items.commonMistake: US past spelling may be “canceled”; UK commonly uses “cancelled.”

visual.altEn: A scheduled class is crossed out and will not happen.
visual.altJa: 予定していた授業に取り消しの印がついています。

items.exampleSentence: Heavy rain delayed our flight.
items.exampleJapanese: 大雨で飛行機が遅れました。
items.commonMistake: Use “be delayed,” not “be delay.”

visual.altEn: A train’s departure moves from 9:00 to 9:30.
visual.altJa: 電車の出発が9時から9時30分へ遅れています。

items.japanese: 予約する・取っておく
items.exampleSentence: I reserved a table by the window.
items.exampleJapanese: 窓際の席を予約しました。
items.commonMistake: Reserve a table or room; book is often more conversational.

visual.altEn: A table is set aside for two people at a chosen time.
visual.altJa: 決めた時刻に二人で使えるよう、席を予約しています。

items.exampleSentence: Please confirm your name and address.
items.exampleJapanese: お名前と住所をご確認ください。
items.commonMistake: “Confirm” means establish as correct, not simply look at.

visual.altEn: A person checks an appointment’s date and time and confirms it is right.
visual.altJa: 予約の日付と時刻を確かめ、正しいと確認します。

items.exampleSentence: I prepared a short introduction.
items.exampleJapanese: 短い自己紹介を準備しました。
items.commonMistake: Use “prepare for an event” but “prepare something” without “for.”

visual.altEn: Packing needed items makes someone ready to leave.
visual.altJa: 必要な物を用意し、出発の準備が整います。

items.exampleSentence: They deliver groceries in the evening.
items.exampleJapanese: その店は夕方に食料品を配達します。
items.commonMistake: “Deliver something to someone” is the clearest basic pattern; a double-object pattern is also possible in some contexts.

visual.altEn: An illustration of deliver.
visual.altJa: 配達する・伝えるのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Restart the device after the update.
items.exampleJapanese: 更新後に端末を再起動してください。
items.commonMistake: “Device” is broad; name the phone or tablet when specificity helps.

visual.altEn: A laptop and a mobile phone are two kinds of electronic device.
visual.altJa: ノートパソコンと携帯電話という電子機器。

items.exampleSentence: The text is too small on this screen.
items.exampleJapanese: この画面では文字が小さすぎます。
items.commonMistake: Say “on the screen,” not “in the screen.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of screen.
visual.altJa: 画面のイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: I packed the wrong charger.
items.exampleJapanese: 間違った充電器を荷物に入れました。
items.commonMistake: A charger supplies power; a cable alone may not be a charger.

visual.altEn: An illustration of charger.
visual.altJa: 充電器のイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress BAT; US speech often softens the t.
items.exampleSentence: My battery is very low.
items.exampleJapanese: バッテリー残量がほとんどありません。
items.commonMistake: Say “the battery is low,” not usually “the battery is little.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of battery.
visual.altJa: 電池・バッテリーのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress PASS and connect both parts.
items.exampleSentence: I forgot my password and had to reset it.
items.exampleJapanese: パスワードを忘れたので、再設定しなければなりませんでした。
items.commonMistake: “Reset a password” means choose a new one after losing access. “Forget” describes what happened to your memory.

visual.altEn: A sign-in box hides typed password characters behind dots.
visual.altJa: ログイン画面で、入力したパスワードが点で隠れています。

items.exampleSentence: I created a separate study account.
items.exampleJapanese: 学習用に別のアカウントを作りました。
items.commonMistake: Use “log in to an account,” not “login an account.”

visual.altEn: A personal learning profile has its own name and saved work.
visual.altJa: 自分の名前と学習内容がある個人用アカウント。

items.pronunciationHint: As a verb, stress DATE; as a noun, often stress UP.
items.exampleSentence: Please update the app tonight.
items.exampleJapanese: 今夜アプリを更新してください。
items.commonMistake: “Update” changes existing software; “upgrade” moves to a higher version or plan.

visual.altEn: An installed app changes from an old version to a newer version.
visual.altJa: 入っているアプリを新しいバージョンに更新します。

items.pronunciationHint: As a verb, usually stress LOAD.
items.exampleSentence: Download the worksheet before class.
items.exampleJapanese: 授業前にワークシートをダウンロードしてください。
items.commonMistake: A download moves data to your device; upload sends it away.

visual.altEn: An illustration of download.
visual.altJa: ダウンロードするのイラスト。

items.pronunciationHint: As a verb, usually stress LOAD.
items.exampleSentence: Upload one clear photo of your work.
items.exampleJapanese: 課題の鮮明な写真を1枚アップロードしてください。
items.commonMistake: Do not confuse upload with download.

visual.altEn: A photo moves from a laptop to an online service.
visual.altJa: 写真をパソコンからオンラインへ送っています。

items.exampleSentence: Connect the headphones before the call.
items.exampleJapanese: 通話前にヘッドホンを接続してください。
items.commonMistake: Use “connect to a network” and “connect a device to a network.”

visual.altEn: A cable is plugged into a laptop to connect the devices.
visual.altJa: ケーブルをパソコンにつなぎ、機器を接続しています。

items.exampleSentence: We recycle glass at the community center.
items.exampleJapanese: 地域センターでガラスをリサイクルします。
items.commonMistake: Use “recycle paper” directly. “Recyclable” describes a material; “recycling” names the process.

visual.altEn: An illustration of recycle.
visual.altJa: リサイクルするのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Plan meals carefully to reduce food waste.
items.exampleJapanese: 食品ロスを減らすため、食事をよく計画しましょう。
items.commonMistake: “Waste” is usually uncountable when referring to rubbish broadly.

visual.altEn: An illustration of waste.
visual.altJa: 廃棄物・無駄にするのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Turning off lights saves energy.
items.exampleJapanese: 照明を消すとエネルギーを節約できます。
items.commonMistake: Do not pronounce the g as in “go.”

visual.altEn: An energy meter shows electricity being used to light a bulb.
visual.altJa: 照明が電気を使い、使用量がメーターに表示されています。

items.exampleSentence: The city is working to reduce air pollution.
items.exampleJapanese: 市は大気汚染の削減に取り組んでいます。
items.commonMistake: “Pollution” is uncountable; avoid “pollutions” in general use.

visual.altEn: Smoke from a chimney and exhaust from a car make the air dirty.
visual.altJa: 煙突と車から煙が出て、空気が汚れています。

items.exampleSentence: This plant grows well in a warm climate.
items.exampleJapanese: この植物は暖かい気候でよく育ちます。
items.commonMistake: Weather is short-term; climate describes long-term patterns.

visual.altEn: A globe, many calendar years, and temperatures show weather patterns over a long time.
visual.altJa: 地球と長い年月、気温で長期的な気候を示しています。

items.exampleSentence: Trees protect the path from strong wind.
items.exampleJapanese: 木々が強風から道を守っています。
items.commonMistake: Use “protect something from danger,” not “protect danger.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of protect.
visual.altJa: 守るのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: We can reduce water use at home.
items.exampleJapanese: 家庭で水の使用量を減らせます。
items.commonMistake: “Reduce water use” names what you make smaller. “Reduce by ten percent” gives the amount of the change.

visual.altEn: Less water is used after a change in daily habits.
visual.altJa: 習慣を変えた後、水の使用量が少なくなっています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress USE and finish with voiced /z/.
items.exampleSentence: Reuse the jar to store pencils.
items.exampleJapanese: その瓶を鉛筆入れとして再利用してください。
items.commonMistake: The noun “reuse” may have /s/ at the end; the verb has /z/.

visual.altEn: An empty food jar becomes a useful pencil holder.
visual.altJa: 空き瓶を捨てずに鉛筆入れとして使い直しています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress differs across speakers and varieties. Listen for the stressed syllable in your selected US or UK model.
items.exampleSentence: Clean water is a precious resource.
items.exampleJapanese: きれいな水は貴重な資源です。
items.commonMistake: Use plural “resources” for several materials or sources.

visual.altEn: Water, trees, and sunlight are resources people can use.
visual.altJa: 水・木・日光という、人が利用できる資源。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress STAIN; later syllables are light.
items.exampleSentence: The café uses sustainable packaging.
items.exampleJapanese: そのカフェは持続可能な包装を使っています。
items.commonMistake: Do not use “sustainable” merely to mean popular or modern.

visual.altEn: New trees are planted and grow so a resource can continue into the future.
visual.altJa: 木を植えて育て、将来も資源を使えるようにしています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress CON; later vowels are weak.
items.exampleSentence: I feel more confident after practicing.
items.exampleJapanese: 練習した後はもっと自信が持てます。
items.commonMistake: Say “confident about something” or “confident that…”.

visual.altEn: A prepared speaker stands ready to present without hesitation.
visual.altJa: 準備した話し手が、自信を持って発表しようとしています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress NER; the second vowel is weak.
items.exampleSentence: She felt nervous before her presentation.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女は発表前に緊張していました。
items.commonMistake: “Nervous” describes anxiety; “sensitive” has a different meaning.

visual.altEn: A worried person is about to speak into a microphone.
visual.altJa: マイクの前で、これから話すことに緊張している人。

items.exampleSentence: I am proud of your steady progress.
items.exampleJapanese: あなたの着実な進歩を誇りに思います。
items.commonMistake: Say “proud of,” not “proud for.”

visual.altEn: A person happily holds a certificate they worked to earn.
visual.altJa: 努力して得た賞状を持ち、誇らしく感じている人。

items.kanaReading: ディサポインティッド
items.exampleSentence: We were disappointed by the cancellation.
items.exampleJapanese: 私たちは中止にがっかりしました。
items.commonMistake: Use “disappointed” for a person and “disappointing” for a result.

visual.altEn: A person hoped to win a medal but is sad when it does not happen.
visual.altJa: メダルを期待していたのに得られず、がっかりしている人。

items.exampleSentence: I am grateful for your honest feedback.
items.exampleJapanese: 率直なフィードバックに感謝しています。
items.commonMistake: Say “grateful for something” and “grateful to someone.”

visual.altEn: Someone receives help and smiles warmly at the helper.
visual.altJa: 助けてもらった人が相手に感謝してほほえんでいます。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress CURE; the ending is light.
items.exampleSentence: The children were curious about the new machine.
items.exampleJapanese: 子どもたちは新しい機械に興味津々でした。
items.commonMistake: “Curious” can mean interested or unusual, depending on context.

visual.altEn: A person leans in to examine an unfamiliar puzzle piece.
visual.altJa: 知らないパズルのピースを興味深く観察している人。

items.japanese: 恥ずかしい・気まずい
items.pronunciationHint: Stress BAR and finish with t.
items.exampleSentence: I felt embarrassed when I forgot her name.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女の名前を忘れて恥ずかしく感じました。
items.commonMistake: Use “embarrassed” for a person and “embarrassing” for the situation.

visual.altEn: A person blushes after accidentally spilling a drink in front of others.
visual.altJa: 人前で飲み物をこぼし、頬を赤くして気まずそうな人。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress LIEVED and keep the final d.
items.exampleSentence: We were relieved to hear the good news.
items.exampleJapanese: 良い知らせを聞いてほっとしました。
items.commonMistake: Use “relieved to hear the news” or “relieved that everyone is safe.” “Relieved about” also works with an appropriate noun.

visual.altEn: Worry about something missing changes to calm after it is found.
visual.altJa: なくし物を心配していた人が、見つけてほっとします。

items.japanese: いら立った・もどかしい
items.kanaReading: フラストレイティッド
items.exampleSentence: He was frustrated with the slow connection.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼は接続の遅さにいら立っていました。
items.commonMistake: Use “frustrated” for a person and “frustrating” for a cause.

visual.altEn: A person is annoyed because a slow computer will not finish a task.
visual.altJa: パソコンが遅く作業が進まないため、もどかしく感じている人。

items.pronunciationHint: A pronunciation without /l/ is common in both models. Some speakers pronounce a light /l/.
items.exampleSentence: Take a breath and stay calm.
items.exampleJapanese: 深呼吸して落ち着いてください。
items.commonMistake: “Stay calm” describes your state. Use “calmly” with an action: “speak calmly.”

visual.altEn: An illustration of calm.
visual.altJa: 落ち着いたのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: Compare the two solutions before choosing.
items.exampleJapanese: 選ぶ前に2つの解決策を比較してください。
items.commonMistake: “Compare A with B” and “compare A to B” can both introduce a comparison; explain which similarities or differences you mean.

visual.altEn: Two apples are placed side by side to examine size and colour.
visual.altJa: 二つのりんごを並べ、大きさや色を比べています。

items.pronunciationHint: As a verb, stress TRAST. The noun usually stresses CON.
items.exampleSentence: Contrast the writer’s two main ideas.
items.exampleJapanese: 筆者の2つの主な考えを対比してください。
items.commonMistake: Do not use “contrast” when only listing similarities.

visual.altEn: A bright sunny day and a rainy day highlight a clear difference.
visual.altJa: 晴れた日と雨の日を並べ、違いをはっきり示しています。

items.exampleSentence: Describe what changed in the picture.
items.exampleJapanese: 絵の中で何が変わったか説明してください。
items.commonMistake: Describe something directly; do not add “about.”

visual.altEn: A speaker points to an apple and describes its visible features.
visual.altJa: りんごを指し、見た目の特徴を説明する人。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress SUM and finish with voiced /z/.
items.exampleSentence: Summarize the article in three sentences.
items.exampleJapanese: 記事を3文で要約してください。
items.commonMistake: A summary keeps key ideas, not every detail.

visual.altEn: A long page is condensed to three short key points.
visual.altJa: 長い文章を、三つの短い要点にまとめています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress AN and finish with voiced /z/.
items.exampleSentence: Analyze why the plan succeeded.
items.exampleJapanese: 計画が成功した理由を分析してください。
items.commonMistake: Do not use “analyze about”; analyze takes a direct object.

visual.altEn: A person examines parts of a chart to understand the pattern behind it.
visual.altJa: グラフを部分ごとに調べ、傾向の理由を考えている人。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress EV; the later vowels are weak.
items.exampleSentence: The chart provides evidence for her claim.
items.exampleJapanese: その図は彼女の主張の根拠になります。
items.commonMistake: “Evidence” is uncountable; say “a piece of evidence.”

visual.altEn: A photograph of a footprint provides evidence of what happened.
visual.altJa: 足跡の写真が、何が起きたかを示す証拠になっています。

items.exampleSentence: Give one reason for your choice.
items.exampleJapanese: 選んだ理由を1つ挙げてください。
items.commonMistake: Use “the reason for a decision” or “the reason why…”.

visual.altEn: Rain explains why a person takes an umbrella.
visual.altJa: 雨が降っていることが、傘を持つ理由になっています。

items.japanese: 結果・結果として生じる
items.exampleSentence: The result matched our prediction.
items.exampleJapanese: 結果は私たちの予想と一致しました。
items.commonMistake: Use “result of” for a cause and “result in” for an outcome.

visual.altEn: A planted seed grows into a plant, showing the result of the action.
visual.altJa: 種を植えた結果、植物が育っています。

items.pronunciationHint: Use the voiceless th /θ/, as in “think.”
items.exampleSentence: This method works well for short texts.
items.exampleJapanese: この方法は短い文章に効果的です。
items.commonMistake: Do not voice the th as /ð/ or replace it with d or z.

visual.altEn: A numbered method shows how to fold a shirt.
visual.altJa: シャツをたたむ方法を番号付きの手順で示しています。

items.exampleSentence: In my opinion, the second option is clearer.
items.exampleJapanese: 私の意見では、2つ目の案のほうが明確です。
items.commonMistake: Say “in my opinion,” not “according to my opinion.”

visual.altEn: Different people think different fruits are best.
visual.altJa: 人によって、どちらの果物がよいか考えが違います。

items.exampleSentence: The team discussed my proposal.
items.exampleJapanese: チームは私の提案について話し合いました。
items.commonMistake: A proposal is a developed suggestion, not merely an idea.

visual.altEn: One person presents a written plan for a group to consider.
visual.altJa: 一人が案を書いた紙を示し、グループに提案しています。

items.exampleSentence: The project stayed within budget.
items.exampleJapanese: そのプロジェクトは予算内に収まりました。
items.commonMistake: Use “stay within budget” for keeping to a spending limit, and “go over budget” for spending too much.

visual.altEn: A fixed amount of money is divided between planned expenses.
visual.altJa: 決まった金額を、予定した費用に分けた予算。

items.exampleSentence: Safety is our first priority.
items.exampleJapanese: 安全が私たちの最優先事項です。
items.commonMistake: “Top priority” is natural; avoid redundant “most top priority.”

visual.altEn: The most important task is placed above the others and marked with a star.
visual.altJa: 一番大切な作業をリストの先頭に置き、星で示しています。

items.exampleSentence: We need a simple launch strategy.
items.exampleJapanese: 簡単な立ち上げ戦略が必要です。
items.commonMistake: A strategy is an overall approach; a tactic is one action.

visual.altEn: A planned route connects a starting point to a goal while avoiding an obstacle.
visual.altJa: 障害を避けながら目標に向かう道筋を計画しています。

items.exampleSentence: We review progress every Friday.
items.exampleJapanese: 毎週金曜日に進捗を確認します。
items.commonMistake: “Progress” is uncountable; avoid “progresses” for general advancement.

visual.altEn: More parts of a shared task are complete at each stage.
visual.altJa: 段階が進むごとに、作業の完成した部分が増えています。

items.japanese: フィードバック・意見
items.pronunciationHint: Stress FEED and connect both parts.
items.exampleSentence: Your specific feedback improved the draft.
items.exampleJapanese: 具体的なフィードバックのおかげで下書きが改善しました。
items.commonMistake: “Feedback” is uncountable; avoid “feedbacks.”

visual.altEn: Someone gives specific comments on a learner’s work to help improve it.
visual.altJa: 課題のよい点と直す点を具体的に伝えています。

items.exampleSentence: They negotiated a later delivery date.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼らは配達日を遅らせる交渉をしました。
items.commonMistake: Negotiate “with” a person and “for/about” terms.

visual.altEn: People discuss price and timing before reaching an agreement.
visual.altJa: 値段と日程について話し合い、合意を目指しています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress PROVE and finish with voiced v.
items.exampleSentence: The client approved the final design.
items.exampleJapanese: 顧客は最終デザインを承認しました。
items.commonMistake: Approve a thing directly; approve “of” behavior or an idea generally.

visual.altEn: A decision maker marks a submitted plan as approved.
visual.altJa: 提出された計画に、承認のしるしがついています。
