items.pronunciationHint: Stress VISE and finish with voiced /z/.
items.exampleSentence: Please revise the opening paragraph.
items.exampleJapanese: 冒頭の段落を修正してください。
items.commonMistake: In UK education, “revise” can mean study again; context matters.

visual.altEn: A writer changes and improves a draft with visible edits.
visual.altJa: 下書きの文章を書き直して改善しています。

items.exampleSentence: We will launch the new course in April.
items.exampleJapanese: 4月に新しいコースを開始します。
items.commonMistake: Use “launch a product,” not “open a product.”

visual.altEn: A completed app becomes available to people for the first time.
visual.altJa: 完成したアプリを初めて公開し、使えるようにします。

items.exampleSentence: Could you tell me where to report missing luggage?
items.exampleJapanese: 荷物が届かない場合、どこに届け出ればよいか教えていただけますか。
items.commonMistake: “Luggage” is uncountable; say “a piece of luggage.”

visual.altEn: A suitcase and a travel bag are grouped together as luggage.
visual.altJa: 旅行用のスーツケースとかばんをまとめた荷物。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress PASS and keep the final t.
items.exampleSentence: I had to renew my passport before I could book the trip.
items.exampleJapanese: 旅行を予約する前に、パスポートを更新する必要がありました。
items.commonMistake: Use “renew a passport” when you need a new period of validity. “Update” usually describes changing information.

visual.altEn: An illustration of passport.
visual.altJa: パスポートのイラスト。

items.exampleSentence: We were asked to declare the food we were carrying at customs.
items.exampleJapanese: 税関で、持っていた食品を申告するよう求められました。
items.commonMistake: Use plural-form “customs” for the border service.

visual.altEn: At a border inspection desk, a traveller declares the contents of their luggage.
visual.altJa: 国境の検査窓口で、旅行者が荷物の中身を申告しています。

items.exampleSentence: We changed our destination after the original flight was canceled.
items.exampleJapanese: 最初の便が欠航したので、私たちは目的地を変更しました。
items.commonMistake: A destination is the place you are going, not the route.

visual.altEn: A route ends at a highlighted place where the traveller wants to go.
visual.altJa: 移動ルートの終わりに、行きたい目的地が示されています。

items.exampleSentence: We need to arrange accommodation within walking distance of the station.
items.exampleJapanese: 駅から歩ける範囲で宿泊先を手配する必要があります。
items.commonMistake: “Accommodation” is usually uncountable in UK English.

visual.altEn: A place to stay has a room, bed, and a guest key.
visual.altJa: 泊まる場所に、部屋とベッド、宿泊用の鍵があります。

items.exampleSentence: Could you confirm whether my reservation includes breakfast?
items.exampleJapanese: 私の予約に朝食が含まれるか確認していただけますか。
items.commonMistake: A reservation is the booking record; a reserve is not the noun here.

visual.altEn: A hotel room is booked for specific dates and the booking is confirmed.
visual.altJa: 決まった日付で客室を予約し、予約内容を確認しています。

items.exampleSentence: Our departure was brought forward, so we had to leave the hotel earlier.
items.exampleJapanese: 出発時刻が早まったので、ホテルをもっと早く出なければなりませんでした。
items.commonMistake: Departure is leaving; arrival is reaching the destination.

visual.altEn: An aircraft leaves at the time shown on a departure board.
visual.altJa: 出発案内に表示された時刻に、飛行機が出発します。

items.exampleSentence: Please let the hotel know your estimated time of arrival.
items.exampleJapanese: 到着予定時刻をホテルに知らせてください。
items.commonMistake: “On arrival” means when you reach a place. At an airport, the usual sign is “Arrivals,” and the room is the “arrivals hall.”

visual.altEn: A flight lands and a traveller reaches the arrivals area.
visual.altJa: 飛行機が着陸し、旅行者が到着エリアに着きます。

items.exampleSentence: The platform changed at the last minute, and we nearly missed the train.
items.exampleJapanese: 直前にホームが変更になり、もう少しで電車に乗り遅れるところでした。
items.commonMistake: Use “on the platform,” not “in the platform.”

visual.altEn: A passenger waits on the raised platform beside train doors.
visual.altJa: 乗客が電車のドアの横にあるホームで待っています。

items.pronunciationHint: As a noun, stress TRANS; as a verb, stress FER.
items.exampleSentence: We missed our connection because the airport transfer took longer than expected.
items.exampleJapanese: 空港間の移動が予想以上にかかり、乗り継ぎ便に間に合いませんでした。
items.commonMistake: An airport transfer is transport between an airport and another place. A connection is the next flight or train you catch.

visual.altEn: A shuttle bus takes a traveller between two airports for a connecting flight.
visual.altJa: 乗り継ぎ便のために、バスで空港間を移動しています。

items.japanese: 何とかする・管理する
items.exampleSentence: I managed to finish before the deadline.
items.exampleJapanese: 締め切り前になんとか終えました。
items.commonMistake: Use “manage to do,” not “manage doing,” for succeeding.

visual.altEn: A busy person completes a difficult task before time runs out.
visual.altJa: 忙しい人が、なんとか時間内に難しい作業を終えています。

items.exampleSentence: Try to avoid checking your phone while studying.
items.exampleJapanese: 勉強中に携帯を見るのを避けてみてください。
items.commonMistake: Use “avoid doing,” not “avoid to do.”

visual.altEn: A person changes direction to stay clear of a puddle.
visual.altJa: 水たまりを避けて、進む方向を変えて歩く人。

items.japanese: 余裕がある・購入できる
items.exampleSentence: We cannot afford a longer delay.
items.exampleJapanese: これ以上の遅れは許容できません。
items.commonMistake: Use “afford to do” or “afford something,” not “afford for.”

visual.altEn: Money saved is enough to pay the bicycle’s price.
visual.altJa: 貯めたお金が自転車の値段に足り、購入できる状態。

items.exampleSentence: I recommend taking the earlier train.
items.exampleJapanese: 早い電車に乗ることを勧めます。
items.commonMistake: Use “recommend doing” or “recommend that…,” not “recommend you to do.”

visual.altEn: Someone points out one book as a good choice for a reader.
visual.altJa: 読者に合う一冊の本を、よい選択として勧めています。

items.exampleSentence: She suggested meeting near the station.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女は駅の近くで会うことを提案しました。
items.commonMistake: Use “suggest doing,” not “suggest to do.”

visual.altEn: A person offers a new idea for the group to consider.
visual.altJa: グループに考えてもらうため、新しい案を出す人。

items.exampleSentence: I'd prefer to wait until we have all the details.
items.exampleJapanese: 詳細がすべて分かるまで待ちたいです。
items.commonMistake: Say “prefer A to B,” not “prefer A than B.”

visual.altEn: A person chooses tea over coffee when both are offered.
visual.altJa: 紅茶とコーヒーの両方がある中で、紅茶を好んで選びます。

items.exampleSentence: The finish time depends on the weather.
items.exampleJapanese: 終了時刻は天候によります。
items.commonMistake: Use “depend on,” not “depend of.”

visual.altEn: Whether an outdoor game goes ahead changes with the weather.
visual.altJa: 屋外の試合ができるかは、雨か晴れかによって変わります。

items.exampleSentence: Did you notice the change in tone?
items.exampleJapanese: 口調の変化に気づきましたか。
items.commonMistake: “Notice” is observing; “realize” is understanding a fact.

visual.altEn: A person spots one small error on an otherwise correct page.
visual.altJa: 正しそうな紙の中に、一つの小さな間違いを見つける人。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress RE and finish with voiced /z/.
items.exampleSentence: I realized that I had the wrong date.
items.exampleJapanese: 日付を間違えていたことに気づきました。
items.commonMistake: US spelling is “realize”; UK also accepts “realise.”

visual.altEn: Confusion changes to understanding when a person sees they had the wrong date.
visual.altJa: 日付を取り違えていたと分かり、混乱が理解に変わる人。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress HAN; the ending is weak.
items.exampleSentence: She handled the complaint calmly.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女は苦情に落ち着いて対処しました。
items.commonMistake: Handle a problem directly; do not add “with.”

visual.altEn: A person takes a complaint, works through it, and sorts it out.
visual.altJa: 苦情を聞き、内容を確認して対処する人。

items.exampleSentence: This shortcut makes the process more efficient.
items.exampleJapanese: この近道で作業がより効率的になります。
items.commonMistake: Efficient means using resources well; effective means producing the result.

visual.altEn: The same finished work takes less time with a better process.
visual.altJa: 同じ作業を、改善したやり方で短い時間に終えます。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress FLEX; later vowels are weak.
items.exampleSentence: My work hours are fairly flexible.
items.exampleJapanese: 私の勤務時間はかなり柔軟です。
items.commonMistake: Flexible can describe schedules, materials, or attitudes.

visual.altEn: An appointment can move between two available times.
visual.altJa: 予約の時刻を、都合に合わせて柔軟に動かせます。

items.exampleSentence: We need a reliable internet connection.
items.exampleJapanese: 安定して信頼できるインターネット接続が必要です。
items.commonMistake: Reliable means dependable, not simply accurate.

visual.altEn: A bus arrives at its scheduled time on several consecutive days.
visual.altJa: バスが何日も続けて予定どおりに来て、信頼できることを示します。

items.exampleSentence: Choose language appropriate for the audience.
items.exampleJapanese: 聞き手に適切な言葉を選んでください。
items.commonMistake: Use “appropriate for” a person or purpose; “appropriate to” is also standard in suitable contexts.

visual.altEn: A raincoat suits rainy weather better than sunglasses.
visual.altJa: 雨の日に、サングラスよりレインコートが状況に合っています。

items.exampleSentence: The change produced a significant improvement.
items.exampleJapanese: その変更で大きな改善がありました。
items.commonMistake: Significant may mean important or statistically meaningful; context matters.

visual.altEn: A chart shows a large meaningful improvement rather than a tiny change.
visual.altJa: グラフに、小さな変化ではなく大きな改善が表れています。

items.exampleSentence: Please give one specific example.
items.exampleJapanese: 具体的な例を1つ挙げてください。
items.commonMistake: Specific is more precise than “special.”

visual.altEn: One exact apple is selected from several similar apples.
visual.altJa: 似たりんごが並ぶ中から、特定の一つを指し示しています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress TEM; later vowels are light.
items.exampleSentence: This is only a temporary solution.
items.exampleJapanese: これは一時的な解決策にすぎません。
items.commonMistake: Do not use “temporarily solution”; use adjective “temporary.”

visual.altEn: A sign lasts for a short marked period and is then removed.
visual.altJa: 決まった短い期間だけ掲示され、その後は外される案内。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress PER; later vowels are weak.
items.exampleSentence: The mark is permanent, so use a pencil first.
items.exampleJapanese: その印は消えないので、最初は鉛筆を使ってください。
items.commonMistake: Permanent contrasts with temporary, not with recent.

visual.altEn: A permanent ink mark remains after an attempt to erase it.
visual.altJa: 消そうとしても紙に残る、消えないインクの印。

items.exampleSentence: We're likely to miss the deadline unless we get more help.
items.exampleJapanese: もっと協力を得られなければ、締め切りに間に合いそうにありません。
items.commonMistake: Use “be likely to do” or “It is likely that…”; do not say “I likely go” when you mean “I am likely to go.”

visual.altEn: Most of the forecast shows rain, so a person prepares an umbrella.
visual.altJa: 予報の大部分が雨なので、降りそうだと考えて傘を用意します。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress LIKE; keep the un prefix light.
items.exampleSentence: The plan is unlikely to work without a reliable backup.
items.exampleJapanese: 確実な代替策がなければ、この計画はうまくいきそうにありません。
items.commonMistake: “Unlikely” means improbable, not impossible.

visual.altEn: A hot summer day makes snowfall very improbable.
visual.altJa: 暑い夏の日なので、雪が降る可能性はとても低い場面。

items.exampleSentence: Could you clarify what the final step involves?
items.exampleJapanese: 最後の手順に何が含まれるか明確にしてもらえますか。
items.commonMistake: Clarify an idea directly; “clarify about” is usually unnecessary.

visual.altEn: A confusing instruction becomes a clear three-step instruction that a listener understands.
visual.altJa: 曖昧な指示が三つの明確な手順になり、聞き手が理解します。

items.exampleSentence: The guide emphasizes regular practice.
items.exampleJapanese: そのガイドは継続的な練習を強調しています。
items.commonMistake: US spelling is “emphasize”; UK also uses “emphasise.”

visual.altEn: One important point is highlighted and underlined while someone points to it.
visual.altJa: 大切な一文に下線と強調の印を付けて示しています。

items.exampleSentence: She persuaded the team to test the idea.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼女はその案を試すようチームを説得しました。
items.commonMistake: Use “persuade someone to do something.” “Convince someone to do something” is also common, especially in US English.

visual.altEn: A listener changes from unsure to agreeing after hearing reasons.
visual.altJa: 理由を聞いた相手が、迷いから賛成へ考えを変えます。

items.japanese: 認める・受け取ったと伝える
items.pronunciationHint: Stress the second syllable /ˈnɒl/ (UK) or /ˈnɑːl/ (US). Finish with /ɪdʒ/.
items.exampleSentence: He acknowledged the concern before responding.
items.exampleJapanese: 彼は返答する前に懸念を認めました。
items.commonMistake: The k in “ack” is pronounced, but the written w is silent.

visual.altEn: A person receives a message and signals that they have received and understood it.
visual.altJa: メッセージを受け取り、確かに受け止めたと相手へ示します。

items.exampleSentence: How we respond to criticism can be just as important as the work itself.
items.exampleJapanese: 批判にどう応じるかは、仕事そのものと同じくらい大切なことがあります。
items.commonMistake: Use “respond to,” not “respond someone.”

visual.altEn: An incoming message is followed by a reply going back to the sender.
visual.altJa: 届いたメッセージに対して、送り主へ返事を出しています。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress TRIB in common US speech.
items.exampleSentence: Everyone contributed one practical idea.
items.exampleJapanese: 全員が実用的な案を1つずつ出しました。
items.commonMistake: Use “contribute to a project,” not “contribute for.”

visual.altEn: Each person adds one piece to a shared result.
visual.altJa: 一人ひとりが一つずつ加え、共同の成果に貢献します。

items.exampleSentence: The two classes collaborated on a video.
items.exampleJapanese: 2つのクラスが動画制作で協力しました。
items.commonMistake: Use “collaborate with people on a project.”

visual.altEn: People work together on different parts of one shared creation.
visual.altJa: 一つの制作物に向けて、役割を分けながら協力する人たち。

items.pronunciationHint: Stress SOLVE and finish with voiced v.
items.exampleSentence: We resolved the issue without delaying the launch.
items.exampleJapanese: 開始を遅らせずに問題を解決しました。
items.commonMistake: Resolve suggests a definite solution; it is stronger than discuss.

visual.altEn: A missing solution is found and people reach a settled agreement.
visual.altJa: 解決に必要なものが見つかり、互いに納得して合意します。

items.exampleSentence: Take a minute to reflect on what you learned.
items.exampleJapanese: 学んだことを1分間振り返ってください。
items.commonMistake: Use “reflect on” when thinking carefully about something.

visual.altEn: A person looks back at a past experience and writes down what they learned.
visual.altJa: 過去の体験を振り返り、学んだことを書き留めています。

items.exampleSentence: Good teachers adapt activities to each learner.
items.exampleJapanese: 良い先生は生徒一人ひとりに活動を合わせます。
items.commonMistake: Use “adapt to a situation” and “adapt something for a purpose.”

visual.altEn: A spoon is changed to suit a learner’s needs, making it easier to use.
visual.altJa: 使う人に合うようスプーンを調整し、使いやすくしています。
